data_facts_with_vis_data_meta.paragraph: High blood pressure results from stiff, inflexible arteries. Exercise boosts the amount of blood circulating through your body by up to 25%, which, over time, encourages blood vessels to expand slightly and become more flexible. Exercise also spurs the production of nitric oxide, a molecule that relaxes and widens blood vessels.

facts.fact_content: Exercise boosts the amount of blood circulating through your body by up to 25%.

article_meta_data.title: The many ways exercise helps your heart

data_facts_with_vis_data_meta.paragraph: Both aerobic and muscle-building exercises can lower blood pressure slightly in people with normal blood pressure. If you have high blood pressure (defined as 130/80 mm Hg or higher), the average reductions are greater — between 5 and 7 points in systolic pressure (the first number in the reading). "That's similar to the reduction people experience from taking a blood pressure drug," says Dr. Baggish.

facts.fact_content: Exercise reduces systolic pressure by between 5 and 7 points in people with high blood pressure.
